correctness.rationale: The primary algorithm was reconstructed from its stated fixed-baseline trial sequence, proximal subproblem, sufficient-decrease test, and stopping test. For the scalar quadratic, the surrogate constraint is exactly the original inactive quadratic constraint, so the multiplier vanishes. Direct substitution makes acceptance equivalent to \(2L_i\ge a+\beta\) and makes the stopping test equivalent to \(C_*|z^k|\le\tau\). The radius condition prevents projection clipping, the KL premise holds exactly with exponent \(1/2\), and the exceptional case \(L_*=a\) is separated. The finite verifier checks a representative instance but is not used as proof of the general identities.

value.rationale: The result turns a qualitative inner-loop upper bound into an exact sharpness theorem on a natural admissible quadratic and shows that the same worst-case number of rejected proximal subproblems can recur at every outer iteration solely because of baseline reset. Since the source notes that each constrained proximal subproblem may itself require a conic solve, the exact rejected-solve count is algorithmically meaningful. The family-specific warm-start comparison quantifies the avoidable repeated calibration work without claiming a general modification theorem.
